top_story: US-Iran tensions that began with Trump’s March threat against Iran’s power grid have sharpened into direct Gulf hostilities by late June, with strikes and counterstrikes involving Bahrain and Kuwait putting an interim peace arrangement and any stable reopening of the Strait of Hormuz at risk. This escalation reinforces a wider regional pattern in which coercive military signaling overrides fragile de-escalation efforts and pushes nearby societies toward renewed economic and security shock. In Gaza, that same erosion of restraint is visible in Israeli attacks on displaced civilians in beach tents on 25 June and a 1 July drone strike near a hospital and fuel station that killed three Palestinians despite a declared ceasefire. The combined picture is of a region where ceasefire language no longer reliably limits force, leaving civilians to absorb the costs of both interstate brinkmanship in the Gulf and sustained Israeli violence in Gaza.
